name: Lil Wayne
notes: The bounce-raised rapper who turns the archetype minor. ⛔ **The one parameter that separates this from its parent is modality:** the research says "minor throughout" where `nola-bounce` is bright major/mixolydian, so `session.scales` and the whole `chords.progressionFamilies` list are lower-case, and the Auto-Tune singing era is carried by the stated `i–VI–III–VII` family. ⚠ **The Carter-era half-time band (72–86, = 144–172) is deliberately not modelled here.** The archetype's one defining parameter is `halfTime: false`; a half-time kit with the clap on 3 is a different lane, and the research puts those records on "trap-adjacent 808 kits" rather than on Mannie's. What this model holds is the 92–102 straight Mannie-era material, and the later material's *harmony* — which is the part that survives the tempo change. ⛔ **`drums.bass808.role` flips to `bassline`, which is the sharpest single override in this file.** The parent deliberately runs a two-voice low end — a `counter_riff` 808 under an `independent_riff` played Moog — because Mannie played bass. Wayne's paragraph says the opposite in as many words: "long-decay 808 root as the **only** bass". `role: "bassline"` is the engine's statement that the 808 *is* the bass, so `bass::generate` returns an empty lane and the low end is one voice rather than two. `slideProb` rises to 0.22 from the parent's 0.06 because "slides appear on the later material" — how often is inferred; that they appear is not. ⚠ **`arrangement.sectionBars.verse` is the load-bearing parameter and it is the sourced one.** He "freestyle[s] rhymes while recording over an instrumental, as opposed to writing down his lyrics", so verse lengths are irregular (12–32 bars) — this model reaches six of them where the parent reaches five, and none of them is a plain 16. ⚠ INFERRED, and why this is `medium` rather than the research's high-medium: the tempo band is marked [LOW-CONF] in the research, and the key list, every velocity, the `melody.intervals` split and the `hihat` weights are extrapolated from the lane rather than sourced. ⚠ `snareRoll.pitchWalk` is inherited: nothing in the research says how these producers pitch a roll. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2,4], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
